title: self-declaration-token-flow-for-lightweight-security-exchange-and-pricing-credits
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight self-declaration exchange that lets enterprise buyers submit a minimal, structured security declaration which maps automatically to SIG/CAIQ questions and emits a signed 'Self-Declaration Token' that sales and legal can attach to RFP responses. Pair the flow with a short pricing credit experiment: customers who submit the token receive a one-time onboarding credit or reduced due-diligence hours to accelerate contract close. Goal is to reduce manual effort in preliminary security reviews while preserving auditability and escalation to full attestation when needed.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint that accepts structured declarations (JSON schema) and returns a signed token
Automatic mapping layer that translates user inputs to SIG/CAIQ boolean answers with confidence scores
UI flow in Console for customers to fill and submit the declaration (mobile + desktop)
Signed tokens stored in audit log with KMS-backed signing key and tamper-proof metadata
Manual verification path for answers flagged as low-confidence, with assignment to SOC/SE queue
Pricing experiment flag that applies onboarding credit when a token is issued
Legal and Security sign-off on wording and acceptable scope for 'self-declaration' in contracts
milestones: Pilot with 10 customers and pricing credits: 2026-04-10
Evaluate experiment and decide next steps: 2026-04-25
metrics: Reduction in initial manual questionnaire hours (target: 60%)
Pilot conversion lift for onboarding (target: +12% win rate)
Number of tokens issued in pilot, percent escalated to manual review
consequences_and_risks: Risk that self-declaration will not be accepted by some enterprise procurement/legal teams
Potential for customers to unintentionally misrepresent controls; need for clear disclaimers and escalation
Overhead to maintain accurate SIG/CAIQ mapping as frameworks evolve
Billing/credit abuse if tokens are requested purely to receive pricing benefit; require verification thresholds
notes: 2026-02-22 - Initial scoping: team agreed lightweight flow is acceptable for mid-market; enterprise legal requested mandatory escalation for high-risk answers.
2026-03-01 - Design review: pushed for combined UI + API first so partners (SEs) can script submissions; DES suggested audit visibility per-token.
2026-03-04 - Security meeting: require KMS-based signing and retain full response payload for 2 years; Priya flagged need for revocation endpoint.
2026-03-07 - Pricing ops: propose 1 free onboarding credit (up to $5k equivalent) tied to first-time token issuance for pilot customers; finance needs tracking event.
2026-03-09 - Decision: pilot scoped to 10 customers from sales pipeline with historical questionnaire delays > 2 weeks; ENG to prioritize mapping service and signing microservice (ENG-23456).
